key_insight: Brain-predicted age difference (brain-PAD) is a transdiagnostic marker that captures neurodegeneration-related brain changes better than global atrophy alone in several disorders.
clinical_relevance: Brain-PAD may help distinguish patients from controls and track cognitive decline across Alzheimer’s disease, frontotemporal dementia, and multiple sclerosis, complementing conventional MRI volume measures.
method: Compared brain-PAD with brain parenchymal fraction (BPF) across AD, FTD, MS, and PD.
Tested whether brain-PAD improved patient-vs-control classification and related to cognition cross-sectionally and longitudinally.
Mapped voxel-wise structural correlates to see which regional atrophy patterns contributed to brain-PAD.
evidence_signal: In transdiagnostic analyses, brain-PAD added explanatory value beyond BPF for diagnosis and cognition in AD, FTD, and MS, with less clear benefit in PD.
watch_item: Brain-PAD is promising but requires careful validation across disease types, scanners, and clinical settings before routine use.
paper_title: The value of brain age as a transdiagnostic biomarker of neurodegeneration
